newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BLANC INSPIRES FRANCE TO 4-0 WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLANC INSPIRES FRANCE TO 4-0 WIN.

text.p: Barcelona defender Laurent Blanc inspired France to a 4-0 victory over Turkey in a friendly international on Wednesday, taking the 1998 World Cup hosts' unbeaten run under coach Aime Jacquet to 30 matches.

Blanc, brilliant in defence and attack, made a run through the middle in the 33rd minute to take a superb lofted pass from captain Didier Deschamps which beat the Turkish offside trap and chipped over goalkeeper Rustu Recber for his 11th goal in 56 internationals.

Less than two minutes later Youri Djorkaeff turned to lob an equally fine ball into the path of Marseille midfielder Reynald Pedros, who brought it down brilliantly with his left foot and lobbed the advancing Rustu.

The fine understanding Zinedine Zidane and Djorkaeff have built brought the third goal when the Juventus midfielder sent the Internazionale forward through to round Rustu and score five minutes after the break.
Substitute winger Robert Pires scored the fourth with a lob from way out on the right seven minutes from time for his first goal in his second international.
Blanc steadied the French defence early in the match when the nippy Turks broke through to create several chances, only to stumble against the Barcelona rock.
The Turks, beaten 2-1 away by Belgium in their only World Cup qualifier so far, were unlucky not to score.

Monaco goalkeeper Fabien Barthez, winning his third cap in place of Bernard Lama who is recovering from cartilage surgery, made two successive saves from point blank range from Hakan Sukur and substitute Saffet Sancakli in the 57th minute.
Barthez also turned a searing drive from substitute Mehmet Ozdilek over the bar 15 minutes from time.

France, unsteady in the first quarter of the game with an experimental defence which saw midfielder Christian Karembeu uncomfortable at right back, settled when Auxerre's Sabri Lamouchi went off with an ankle injury in the 23rd minute.
Guingamp's Vincent Candela come on for his first cap at left back, Liliam Thuram crossed to his preferred right flank and Karembeu moved up into midfield.
The change virtually ended the runs down the left of Turkey's Euro 96 success Abdullah Ercan, who found Thuram a much harder nut to crack.
"The match had two parts and we were lucky not to go behind," said Jacquet, happy his new players had fitted in well.
"The demands of the World Cup are such you always have to be on top and there is in these young men a real dynamism."

France - 16-Fabien Barthez; 17-Christian Karembeu, 4-Alain Goma, 5-Laurent Blanc, 15-Lilian Thuram (12-Martin Djetou 76th); 14-Sabri Lamouchi (2-Vincent Candela 23rd), 7-Didier Deschamps, 19-Zinedine Zidane, 8-Reynald Pedros (3-Franck Gava 66th); 6-Youri Djorkaeff, 11-Patrice Loko (13-Robert Pires 71st).

Turkey - 1-Rustu Recber; 2-Recep Cetin, 4-Bulent Korkmaz, 5-Alpay Ozalan; 7-Arif Erdem (13-Saffet Sancakli 46th), 10-Tolunay Kafkas (Erkan Avseren 71st), 3-Ogun Temizkanoglu, 11-Celil Sagir (17-Serdar Toprakte 60th), 6-Abdullah Ercan; 8-Unal Karaman (15-Oguz Cetin 36th), 9-Hakan Sukur (16-Mehmet Ozdilek 63rd).
